pins: The slug algorithm, -N suffixes, Same-1 after three Same headings giving same-1-1, setext h1 and h2.
id="" then -1 and on; only text and code_inline enter the title; CJK, fractions, superscripts and dotted numbers; a tab is dropped.

Python lower() of the whole title (the final sigma becomes ς), İ, ß and astral letters, combining marks dropped from slugs, \x1c \x85 and U+3000 stripped Python-style at heading and paragraph edges, U+FEFF kept by strip and dropped by the slug.
The inline allowlist exactly: br forms, bare sup/sub/kbd, orphan closers, comments vanish, everything else escaped.
Anchor grammar 1..100 characters; 101 dropped; bad ids dropped; an unterminated comment is text; indent 3 is still a block.
Line forms, summary text through Python html.escape (' becomes '), a stray closer dropped, an unclosed opener forced open and closed at the end.
Details lines interrupt a paragraph, sit in a list item or a blockquote, and are code at indent 4.
The codehilite wrapper and data-line; stripnl plus one newline; info split on a space only; unknown languages are plain text.
An empty fence renders one newline inside the wrapper.
An unclosed fence runs to the end of the document.
Indented code is <pre data-line><code> with no codehilite; hard and soft break forms; \| outside a table is untouched.
Figure shape, Python-escaped source, 'mermaid extra' and ' mermaid' are figures and 'Mermaid' is not, figures in a list or blockquote, meta.figures and meta.mermaidKinds.
The caption rule: a caption is one emphasis span, so a two-span paragraph stays a paragraph (ruling C25); non-captions stay paragraphs.

All five kinds, uppercase only, the marker-only alert,
after the marker, a nested alert not converted, an alert inside a plain blockquote converted, data-line on the div and none on the rebuilt

.

The wrapper, alignment styles, \\| in table code becomes |, ragged rows padded and truncated,
cells, meta.tables.
Tight versus loose, start before data-line, task-list classes and checkbox attributes, [X] checked.
A loose task list with a fence and a Task heading, as the reading layout reads it.
A byline paragraph led by , a status table, RULE-ID paragraphs.
Footnote markup, fnref1:1, the backref glyph, an inline note with no data-line, an undefined reference stays text.

The dl strip, list joining with nested items skipped, a block list, a YAML anchor and alias, a duplicate key (last value wins, first position kept), ' through Python html.escape, the hidden-token leading newline, meta.front and meta.frontList.
Departure PD2 (ruled in Task 9): null, booleans, `flag: yes` staying `yes`, floats, dates and datetimes, nested list items skipped, html escaping, and 500-code-point truncation.
Four dashes open and close front matter; departure PD3 on its meta (Task 9).
A ... line closes front matter; departure PD3 on its meta (Task 9).
The rest of the opening line is unchecked (--- x opens); departure PD3 on its meta (Task 9).
Unclosed front matter is ordinary Markdown: a rule and paragraphs.
Front matter only at line 0: a later --- block is a rule and a setext heading.
A leading rule swallows the text up to the next --- as front matter, which renders nothing.
YAML that does not parse renders nothing, leaving the leading newline.
A list at the YAML root renders nothing, and meta.front is null.
validateLink, data:image allowed, normalizeLink (<a b> becomes a%20b), title escaping, alt flattening, image sources for scanRefs.
Escapes, � and � become U+FFFD, NUL normalisation, strikethrough, emphasis edges, thematic breaks.
An empty document renders the empty string.
A whitespace-only document renders the empty string.
22 nested > render 20 blockquotes (maxNesting 20).
An end-to-end spec: In short, numbered sections, a Mermaid figure with a caption, a decision table, an alert, a promise-delta style fence, Where things stand.
CRLF HTML matches LF HTML; departure PD3 on its meta (Task 9).
A leading BOM: the reference renders the front matter as body text; departure PD4 (Task 9).
Script, style, iframe, div, table and svg tags in inline, block, list and blockquote positions are all escaped text.
No on* attribute reaches the output from img, sup, kbd, br, image titles, table cells or a details line.
javascript:, vbscript:, file: and non-image data: never become an href or src, in any case, entity-encoded, as autolinks, reference definitions or images.
Only [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,100} ids are emitted; quotes, spaces, look-alike letters and 101 characters vanish; markup after a comment is escaped.
Fifty stray closers dropped, fifty unclosed openers forced open and closed, attribute forms escaped, summary text escaped including U+2028.
The language class only from the registry; info-string markup never reaches an attribute; Mermaid and code source are escaped text.
__proto__, constructor, toString and prototype keys are ordinary keys.
40 keys, 500 code points per value, 50 list items in the strip and 300 in meta, astral characters at both cuts.
Nine levels of aliases (9^9 leaves if expanded) load as shared references and render in bounded time.
Language-specific YAML tags fail the load, so nothing renders.
A front-matter block of 20000 code points or more is not loaded, so nothing renders and meta.front is null.
Markup in keys and values is escaped.
Ids that name DOM or object properties are emitted exactly by the slug and anchor grammars, and nothing more.
Alert spoofs stay text, 25 nested alerts stay bounded, and a caption carries escaped text only.
An id comment after a blockquote that a details line ends is still an anchor: the comment search covers the whole document even when its first use comes from inside the quote.
Ten thousand nested blockquote markers: maxNesting (20) bounds the depth.
4096 emphasis openers with no closer stay text in linear time.
4096 emphasis closers with no opener stay text in linear time.
4096 nested link brackets stay text in linear time.
4096 backtick runs pair into code spans in linear time.
Emphasis and strong emphasis nested 100 deep each.
90000 thematic breaks: a bounded output ratio.
A table with a 2000-column header and one body row stays balanced.
A 2000-column header with 2000 one-cell rows: the padding stops at the autofill limit.
1000 small tables, each wrapped and balanced.
10000 unclosed details lines: 64 are forced open and closed at the end, the rest are escaped text (ruling C21, departure PD8).
20000 equal headings get the ids a, a-1, a-2 and on, from the memoised uniquifier.
10000 references to one footnote, each with its own back-reference id.
DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES + 1 bytes, a two-byte character at the end: nothing is parsed and the html is empty.
10000 distinct images: scanRefs keeps the first 512 and says it cut the list.
About 200 KB each of quote and backslash runs in Python and template openers in TypeScript: highlighting stays bounded.
20000 unterminated comment openers, one per line, stay text in linear time.
40000 unterminated inline comment openers on one line stay text in linear time.
20000 images whose alt text opens a comment, each followed by an unterminated <!--: each inline text keeps its own comment search, so the paragraph's is never evicted and the time stays linear.
8000 <!-- lines that all reach one closing line with 50000 characters before its --> and 50000 spaces after: the closing line is read once, not once per <!--.
Four tables that each reach markdown-it's 65536 empty-cell limit: the limit holds for the whole document, so the html stays bounded.
A 30000-character line in an ini, a java, a typescript and a javascript fence: a fence with a line over 256 code units is escaped text, never highlighted, so no grammar spends quadratic time on it.
A java fence of 4096 lines of 255 characters (1 MiB): a fence past the document's 256 KiB highlighting budget is escaped text.
100000 unclosed <sup> tags: 64 nest and the rest are escaped text (ruling C21, departure PD8).
A 4000-character destination defined once and used 100000 times (304 KB) would render 200 MB of html: it stops at the 16 MiB html bound with outcome output-over-limit (ruling C20, departure PD8).

600 lines of `$ ${` in a shell fence (3 KB): a fence over 256 characters is highlighted one line at a time (ruling C24), so the html stays linear, 22.7 times the input; highlighted as one block it is 2110 times (6.4 MB).
A 128-line ini fence of `\"` runs, 127 pairs and a backslash a line (32 KB): highlighted one line at a time (ruling C24), so the time stays linear, 34 ms; highlighted as one block it took 2.9 s.

400 `<script></script>` lines in a javascript fence (7 KB): highlighted one line at a time (ruling C24), the html is 1.7 times the input; highlighted as one block it is 10.3 times. This one is held by its output bound: the time the same shape costs as one block (seconds) needs about 256 KiB, more than the 8 MiB total of generated inputs can carry.

8000 inline notes `^[a]` in one paragraph (32 KB): the footnote tail appends each note once (ruling C26), so the time stays linear, 93 ms; the plugin's own tail copies the token array once per note and took 2.8 s.

7000 ordinary `[^n]` references, each with its definition (124 KB): the footnote tail appends each note once (ruling C26), so the time stays linear, 71 ms; the plugin's own tail copies the token array once per note and took 2.0 s.
